sourceRegulation: California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), Cal. Civ. Code 1798.100-1798.199, as amended by CPRA, plus CPPA regulations 11 CCR 7000 et seq. (incl. 2025 ADMT / risk-assessment / cybersecurity-audit rules effective 2026-01-01)
note: Field names inferred from the Transformation Bridge UI. Confirm against the real import schema before load. 'ccpaCitations', 'complianceDate', and 'sdlcGates' are extension fields for traceability. Several standards are conditional on the GLBA-exemption analysis (ccpa-001) and on business thresholds — see INTEGRATION-NOTES.

standards.whatItMeans: Determine whether Meridian is a 'business' under any threshold, and analyze which personal information is exempt as GLBA-covered versus in-scope. The GLBA exemption is information-level, not entity-level, so non-GLBA PI (web visitors, prospects, marketing, employees/applicants, B2B contacts) remains subject to the CCPA.

Inventory and classify personal information and the specific sensitive-PI categories (SSN/IDs, financial credentials, precise geolocation, health, biometric, sexual orientation, etc.) so notice, opt-out, limit-use, security, and retention controls can be scoped.
At or before collection, disclose the categories of PI and SPI collected, the purposes, retention periods, and whether the information is sold or shared.
Maintain a comprehensive privacy policy describing rights, categories, purposes, and disclosures, updated at least every 12 months.
Provide categories and specific pieces of PI, sources, purposes, and recipients on a verifiable request; look-back of at least 12 months; respond within 45 days.
Delete a consumer's PI on a verifiable request and direct service providers and contractors to delete it, subject to statutory exceptions.
Correct inaccurate personal information on a verifiable request, using commercially reasonable efforts.
Provide a clear 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information' mechanism and stop selling or sharing on request. 'Sharing' specifically covers disclosure for cross-context behavioral advertising.
Detect and honor browser/device opt-out preference signals such as Global Privacy Control as a valid request to opt out of sale/sharing.

standards.standard: Right to Limit Use of Sensitive PI
standards.whatItMeans: Provide a 'Limit the Use of My Sensitive Personal Information' mechanism and restrict SPI use to what is necessary to provide the requested goods/services.

Where ADMT substantially replaces human decision-making in a significant decision (e.g., automated underwriting, pricing, claims), provide a pre-use notice, an opt-out, access to information about the logic and outcome, and an appeal path. Crosswalk to GDPR Art. 22 and the EU AI Act.
standards.responsibleRole: Privacy Officer / Chief Actuary / Enterprise Architect

standards.whatItMeans: Do not discriminate against consumers for exercising rights; any financial incentive or price/service difference must be permitted, disclosed, and reasonably related to the value of the data.
Offer at least two request methods, verify the requester's identity, acknowledge within 10 business days, and respond within 45 calendar days (extendable once by 45) with required disclosures.
Collection, use, retention, and sharing of PI must be reasonably necessary and proportionate to the purposes disclosed to the consumer; no use for incompatible purposes without notice.
Disclose and enforce retention periods for each category of PI and SPI; do not retain longer than reasonably necessary for the disclosed purpose.

Implement reasonable security procedures and practices appropriate to the PI. Note the private right of action for breaches of nonencrypted/nonredacted PI caused by failure to maintain reasonable security (statutory damages $100-$750 per consumer per incident).
Identify SPI, honor limit-use requests, and restrict secondary uses; apply heightened safeguards to health, biometric, financial, and precise-geolocation data common in insurance.

Bind service providers, contractors, and third parties with the required contractual terms limiting use to specified purposes, prohibiting unauthorized sale, requiring deletion/flow-down, and permitting compliance verification.

Conduct and document a written risk assessment before high-risk processing (selling/sharing PI, processing SPI, ADMT for significant decisions, training ADMT, or automated inference of sensitive traits); submit documentation to the CPPA from April 1, 2028.

Complete an annual independent cybersecurity audit and submit a certification to the CPPA on the revenue-phased schedule (over $100M: first certification by April 1, 2028 covering 2027), annually thereafter.
Obtain opt-in consent to sell or share PI of consumers under 16 (the consumer for ages 13-15; a parent/guardian for under 13).
Maintain records of consumer requests and how they were handled for at least 24 months; large processors must compile and disclose request metrics.
